title: Access Observability and Evidence Playbook
author: Priya Nambiar
content:
Overview
-------
This playbook defines a unified operational approach for observing access activity, collecting preservation-grade evidence, and demonstrating compliance for model-serving and control-plane systems. It bridges RBAC and authentication, audit logging pipelines, data residency/retention rules, secure SDLC touchpoints, incident response steps, and exception handling.

Scope
-----
Applies to:
- Control plane services (authz, identity, entitlement APIs)
- Model-serving endpoints and inference gateways
- Audit log ingestion, transformation, and archival systems
- Security incident response and forensics teams
- Compliance evidence requests (internal and external auditors)

Not in scope: end-user application business logs (refer to product teams for PII-sensitive app logs).

Key principles
--------------
- Minimal transformation: preserve original log payloads for forensic integrity.
- Chain-of-custody: every extracted artifact must have metadata (exporter, timestamp, verifier).
- Residency-aware packaging: evidence must respect tenant/data residency constraints.
- Time-to-evidence targets: initial evidence snapshot < 2 hours from triage; complete package < 72 hours.
- Role separation: collectors should not be the same owners who approve exceptions.

Definitions
-----------
- Evidence artifact: A preserved item used in an investigation (log segments, DB snapshots, KMS access records, RBAC entitlement exports).
- Custodian: Team responsible for collection and packaging (usually SecOps/Forensics).
- Verifier: Independent reviewer who attests to integrity and completeness.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Custodian: Security - Forensics (primary)
- Data residency questions: Legal & Privacy (escalate)
- RBAC query support: Identity Platform team
- Long-term archive owner: Compliance Team (retention schedule admin)
- Incident commander: defined per incident (see incident-response-security runbooks)

Evidence taxonomy (catalog)
---------------------------
Use the following canonical artifact types and minimal attributes when packaging evidence. Treat this table as the export schema for each artifact.

| Artifact type | Example sources | Required metadata | Suggested retention class |
|---------------|-----------------|-------------------|---------------------------|
| Authz events | OAuth2 token exchanges, PDP decisions | request_id, user_id, client_id, decision, timestamp, raw_payload_hash | hot (90d) then cold (7y) |
| API access logs | Inference requests, metadata | request_id, model_id, latency_ms, src_ip, tenant_id, timestamp | hot (30d) then cold (3y) |
| Entitlement snapshots | RBAC role assignments, group membership | snapshot_time, exporter, object_count, export_hash | immutable (7y) |
| KMS access records | KMS decrypt/sign calls | key_id, principal, operation, timestamp, request_id | restricted (7y) |
| Audit pipeline traces | Delivery failures, transform records | pipeline_run_id, offsets, raw_offsets, timestamp | hot (90d) |

Retention and residency rules (summary)
--------------------------------------
- Default retention classes: hot (30–90 days), cold (1–7 years), immutable (7+ years).
- Tenant-specific residency: if tenant data is subject to in-region residency, package artifacts into region-specific archives and route to region archives.
- Legal hold: when Legal issues a hold, the Compliance Team moves artifacts to immutable storage and extends retention until hold release.
- Redaction policy: do not redact original logs in the evidence store; create a redacted copy for sharing with external parties.

Audit log collection — standard operating procedure
--------------------------------------------------
1. Triage and scope selection
   - Incident commander identifies systems and time ranges.
   - Custodian logs the triage scope in the incident tracker with a unique evidence_id.
2. Live export (for short retention sources)
   - Use authenticated export service (audit-exporter) to pull raw segments.
   - Command example (control plane):
     sh -c "audit-exporter export --service=authz --start=2026-02-25T12:00:00Z --end=2026-02-25T12:45:00Z --out=/tmp/evidence/${EVIDENCE_ID}/authz.raw.ndjson"
   - Hash the file immediately: sha256sum authz.raw.ndjson > authz.raw.ndjson.sha256
3. Entitlement snapshot
   - Export role/permission state using identity tooling:
     curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${EXPORT_TOKEN}" "https://identity.internal/export/entitlements?snapshot_time=2026-02-25T12:00:00Z" -o entitlements.json
   - Record exporter identity and time in exporter.metadata.txt
4. KMS and secrets access logs
   - Request time-bound audit export from KMS audit store. If accessing cloud-managed KMS, use the provider's export job and note job_id.
   - Preserve provider-signed manifests.
5. Packaging
   - Place artifacts under evidence/<evidence_id>/raw/ and metadata under evidence/<evidence_id>/meta/
   - Generate a package manifest (manifest.json) with file entries and SHA256 checksums.
6. Verification and sealing
   - Independent verifier computes checksums and signs manifest with an internal GPG key.
   - Move package to region-appropriate immutable bucket: s3://evidence-immutable/<region>/<year>/<evidence_id>.tar.gz

Incident response evidence workflow (timelines & responsibilities)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
- T+0 (discovery): Incident commander assigns evidence_id and custodian.
- T+2h (initial snapshot): Custodian produces minimal set (authz events + API logs for window) and uploads to secure staging.
- T+24h (complete set): Full pipeline + entitlement snapshots + KMS call records collected.
- T+72h (audit package): Verified, sealed package delivered to Compliance and Incident Review board.

RBAC validation and live forensic queries
---------------------------------------
- Quick entitlement dump (role assignments for user@example.com):
  curl -s "https://identity.internal/admin/roles?user=user@example.com" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" | jq . > role-dump-user.json
- Membership graph export (recommended for triage):
  identity-cli graph-export --user user@example.com --format=graphml --out=user-graph.graphml
- Note: All ad-hoc queries must be logged automatically in the audit pipeline. If permissive query tooling is used, mark it in the evidence manifest as investigator_query=true.

Secure SDLC handoffs for evidence readiness
------------------------------------------
- Release pipelines must include structured audit metadata (build_id, commit_sha, deploy_target) emitted to the audit stream at deploy time.
- Pre-production can be excluded from long-term retention by default; evidence collection for incidents in pre-prod must be approved and mirrored to an evidence store with a documented justification.
- Change control: any infra change that affects log format or offsets must be accompanied by migration notes and a schema mapping document retained with the evidence.

Exception handling and risk approvals
------------------------------------
1. Short-term exception (e.g., 1–14 days): manager-level approval logged in the exception register with rationale and compensating controls.
2. Medium-term (15–90 days): Security + Legal approval required. Attach mitigation plan and monitoring.
3. Permanent exception: only Governance Board can approve; must include an evidence-retrieval playbook specific to that exception.

Packaging checklist for auditors
-------------------------------
- manifest.json (file list + sha256 + exporter identity)
- timeline.txt (actions taken, with UTC timestamps and personnel IDs)
- raw artifacts (logs, snapshots, pipeline traces)
- access_control_list.txt (who had access to the package)
- redacted_copies (if PII present)
- verifier.signature (GPG-signed manifest)

Chain-of-custody template
-------------------------
- Evidence ID: EVIDENCE-2026-000123
- Collected by: Priya Nambiar (sec-forensics)
- Collected at: 2026-02-25T14:08:22Z
- Storage location (staging): s3://evidence-staging/us-west-2/EVIDENCE-2026-000123
- Sealed at: 2026-02-26T02:12:11Z
- Sealed by (verifier): Marta Iglesias
- Archive location: s3://evidence-immutable/us-west-2/2026/EVIDENCE-2026-000123.tar.gz

Appendix A — Example manifest.json (minimal)
-------------------------------------------
{
  "evidence_id": "EVIDENCE-2026-000123",
  "created_at": "2026-02-25T14:10:00Z",
  "exporter": "audit-exporter v1.3.2 (exporter-priya)",
  "files": [
    {"path": "raw/authz.raw.ndjson", "sha256": "<sha256-hash>"},
    {"path": "raw/entitlements.json", "sha256": "<sha256-hash>"}
  ]
}

Appendix B — Quick triage play (TL;DR)
-------------------------------------
1. Assign incident commander and evidence_id.
2. Run audit-exporter for the 30-minute window around suspicious time.
3. Export entitlement snapshot.
4. Seal and upload to staging, notify verifier.
